Chokwe Antar Lumumba, the mayor of Jackson, Mississippi, pleaded guilty to a conspiracy count in a federal bribery scheme after taking a $50,000 bribe from undercover FBI agents posing as developers in exchange for fast-tracking a project. He has been disbarred by the Mississippi Supreme Court, and awaits sentencing. His co-defendants — former Hinds County DA Jody Owens and former councilman Aaron Banks — have already been sentenced to federal prison.

Sources: U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of Mississippi; The Grio; Mississippi Today.

niche.title: Haitian National Pleads Guilty to $7M Massachusetts SNAP Fraud & Selling Donated Relief Meals
niche.description: 25-year-old Saul Alisme pleaded guilty in Boston federal court to trafficking nearly $7 million in SNAP benefits through two tiny Mattapan "ghost stores" with almost no real groceries. Prosecutors say he exchanged EBT cards for cash and liquor—and even sold donated MannaPack charity meals meant for starving children overseas. He faces up to five years in federal prison and deportation when he is sentenced in February 2027.
